Plug a controller in (USB-C on the phone), tap Connect MIDI, and pads 00–07 answer notes 36–43; other notes play the selected synth. Tap Learn, then: tap any pad (drums or synths) and hit a key to give it that note, or touch any slider and turn a knob to put it on that knob. A knob works the slider for whichever pad, layer or effect is open. Select a pad or slider in Learn and tap Unlearn to clear it.

Latency and rate change when audio restarts. That reloads ...Thunder; your song and kit are kept.

Output picks where everything plays: the synth, the tracker and previews. Level is the overall volume after the tracker’s master. Lowest latency answers the pads fastest; Safest uses a bigger buffer if you hear crackles. Rate: Device uses the output’s own rate.

HELP

Getting started

...Thunder has four screens: the Synth, where you build an 8-pad kit; the Tracker, a sequencer that plays that kit; …waves, a modular synth that plays as a layer oscillator; and …chains, where you design modular effects chains for the tracker’s tracks (Phase 1: design and save; audio routing follows). Switch at the top. Everything saves in the browser as you work; Save writes a project file (song and kit) you can keep or move to another device.

How a song fits together

Song (256 rows × 16 tracks of chain numbers) → Chain (up to 16 phrases, each with a transpose) → Phrase (up to 32 rows of note, volume, instrument and three effects) → Inst (which pad a note plays, with transpose, volume, pan, reverse and start). Mixer, FX and Project sit around them.

Chains are hidden by default (⚙ Settings → Hide chains page, or Project → CHAINS): EDIT×2 on an empty song cell makes a block that already holds a phrase, SHIFT+▶ opens that phrase, and EDIT×2 on a filled block makes a unique copy. Set CHAINS to SHOWN for the chain screen; nothing is lost either way.

Arrange (wide screens): the blue overview at the right shows the whole song. Tap a block to go to it, twice to open its phrase, a row number to play from there. Alt-click or hold a block to mute it: the phrase stays in place, silent, so you can drop parts in and out while arranging. TAP: MUTE makes every tap a mute; M does it on the Song screen in KEYS mode.

The screens are laid out as a map: Song ▶ Chain ▶ Phrase ▶ Inst left to right, Project above, Mixer below, FX to the right of the Mixer. You move between them with the screen keys below, the tabs, or the map in the side panel.

Settings

⚙ Settings at the top: on the synth page it holds Kit, MIDI, Export, Skin and Audio (output device, level, latency, rate); in the tracker it opens every Project setting as a touch menu, plus Audio. There you can also turn off Display steps as decimal (row numbers in hex) and change the Text size of the tracker screen. Drag a finger up or down anywhere on the tracker screen to scroll; drag on the cursor's cell to change its value.

Drum pads and synths

The kit has 16 slots. 1–8 are drum pads: one-shots that play their whole sound. 9–16 are synths for melodies and chords (Bass, Pluck, Keys, Pad, Lead, Bell, Organ, Sub to start): a note holds at its sustain level for as long as you hold it, up to the slot’s Max len, then fades over its release when you let go. C-4 plays middle C. In the tracker, instruments 08–0F play the synth slots in a new song.

Chords and polyphony

Tracks 9–16 are polyphonic. Open a phrase from one of them and it shows four note columns, N1–N4, so a row can hold a chord. Notes on these tracks ring over each other, up to 4 at a time per track; a fifth steals the oldest. A note OFF in any note column releases everything on the track. Tracks 1–8 stay one note at a time, and a phrase played there uses only N1.

Two input modes

PAD is a d-pad plus SHIFT, PLAY, OPTION and EDIT, good with a thumb. KEYS is direct entry: type notes, hex and effects, with an on-screen keypad on touch screens. Switch with ⚙ Settings → Input (or Project → INPUT).

One finger is enough. With Sticky keys on, tap SHIFT or OPTION alone and it stays lit for the next button. The command row (Project → COMMANDS) gives every two-key command its own button: change, prev/next, clear, select, copy, cut, paste, play song, and on the SONG screen CLN↓ (clones the block, or the selected blocks, into new numbers on the row below) and CLN (clone): the block under the cursor is copied, phrases and all, to the next free number.

On a computer keyboard in PAD mode: arrows, Shift, Z = OPTION, X = EDIT, Space = PLAY.

Touch

Tap a cell to move there; tap it again to open or add. Drag up or down on the cursor’s cell to change its value; drag elsewhere to scroll.

FX column commands

Each phrase row has three effect columns: a command and a hex value. The info line at the bottom of the screen explains the one under the cursor.

ARParpeggio: the note, +X, +Y semitones
ARCarpeggio pattern (X) and speed in ticks (Y)
CHAchance the note plays
DELdelay the note by XX ticks
GRVgroove for this track: X ticks even, Y odd
GGRgroove for every track
HOPend the phrase; the next starts at row Y
INSplay with instrument XX
KILstop the note after XX ticks
OFFfade the note out after XX ticks
NTHplay on pass Y of every X
RETretrigger every Y ticks, X fades
REPrepeat the last command, adding XX
RNDrandomise the command to the left
RNLRND as a random walk
PSLslide from the last pitch
PBNbend the pitch across the step
PVBvibrato: X speed, Y depth
SEDseed the random numbers
TPOtempo in BPM
TICticks a step from here on (00: the project’s)
TSPtranspose the track from here on
VOLvolume
PITpitch in semitones (signed)
FINfine tune in cents
PLY00 forwards, 01 reversed
STAstart point into the sound
PANpan, 80 is centre

Track effects

Each track and the master have 4 effect slots (FX screen, or EDIT on the Mixer’s FX row): EQ, compressor, reverb, tape delay, saturation, tape, chorus, bitcrush, Rings and Clouds. Renders include them; stems skip the master effects and limiter.

Synth page

Z–/ · Q–PPlay the selected pad chromatically; C-4 is its own pitch. On a synth slot (9–16) notes hold while the keys are down, so you can play chords
− =Octave down / up
Shift 1–8 or ◀ ▶Pick a pad (◀▶ go through all 16 slots)
SpacePlay the pad as it is
Alt 1–7Jump into a tracker screen

Kit ▾ saves and loads kits, Export ▾ writes WAVs for Koala and SunVox, MIDI ▾ connects a controller (notes not mapped to a pad play the selected synth slot, held until note-off), Skin ▾ changes the look.

Files and rendering

Project holds SAVE, SAVE AS and LOAD PROJECT, plus RENDER SONG (a stereo WAV) and RENDER STEMS (a zip with the mix and one WAV per track). In desktop Chrome and Edge, Save writes straight back to the file you opened or last saved; other browsers download a copy, and Save As asks for a name first. The song also saves itself in the browser as you work.

More detail in the README on GitHub.
